newsitem.title: UK: Allied may appeal over mega-merger.
newsitem.headline: Allied may appeal over mega-merger.

text.p: Sir Christopher Hogg, chairman of drinks to pub group Allied Domecq, said on Tuesday the company would appeal to regulatory authorities over a planned 20 billion pound ($32.4 billion) merger between Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness if it's in shareholders interests.

When asked if the group would make representations to regulatory authorities over the merger announced Monday, he replied "Yes. If we think it's in shareholders interests to do so but that is a function of what is going on in particular markets."

He declined to comment further on the question. Earlier in the telephone conference call Hogg said of the planned 24 billion stg merger "It's too early to comment in a nutshell. You will appreciate there is a need to analyse and think about many aspects of what is proposed."

However he said the merger may open up some opportunities for Allied, "there will have to be rearrangements of distribution, sale of brands, management fall out. Not to mention the dislocation that occurs when two companies are put together."
The investment community believes the proposed GrandMet/Guinness merger has left Allied looking weak and vulnerable to a takeover and in need of strategic partners to take on the might of GMG Brands.

Earlier Allied announced first half results which showed a one percent fall in pretax profits at actual exchange rates to 317 million, with profits from its spirits and wine division down two percent at 239 million stg.

"We believe this weak result in spirits really brings Allied to the table," said SocGen analyst Nick Lyall. "The spirits business is struggling but you have to be aware of the takeover speculation now in play."
Allied shares were up 18p at 464p in early trade. ($ = 0.617 British Pounds)
